t: The Triple Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan ruled central Mexico from 1428 through an extensive tribute system.
Tenochtitlan, fed by lake-bed chinampa gardens, held 200,000 or more people, one of the largest cities in the world.
It fell in under two years to smallpox and to a Spanish-led army made up mostly of its own resentful neighbours.
dyk: At the final siege of Tenochtitlan, Cortés's army may have numbered up to 100,000 warriors, of whom fewer than 1,000 were Spaniards.
